title: updatedb cronjob not running. 'locate' works after I manually run updatedb
body:
### Distribution

Mint 22.1

### Package version

6.2.7

### Graphics hardware in use

_No response_

### Frequency

Always

### Bug description

'locate' command produces no results. Run 'sudo updatedb' and then locate produces results. This looks like a daily cron job which I find in /etc/cron.daily/locate. This is a new problem with my upgrade from 21.3 to 22

### Steps to reproduce

As stated above. 

### Expected behavior

'locate' should show me things on my system with the name I indicate

### Additional information

_No response_

comments.body:
Additional information which shows that the cronjob is running upon boot, but is not giving results from user directory, only from system files:
------
/var/cache/locate/locatedb

This file is updated when system booted this morning. However, running 'locate' gives me only results in the system outside my user directory.

Run sudo updatedb

locatedb is updated and is now 3Mb larger than earlier.

running 'locate' with the same argument gives me additional results that exist in my user directory.

Looks like I solved. There is another system besides cron that does this daily update. It is set to run within 12 hours of boot. I changed the setting to 1 hour and that gets the job done before I'm ready to use 'locate'

The file is: /usr/lib/systemd/system/plocate-updatedb.timer 

I changed the line:
    RandomizedDelaySec=12h

to:
RandomizedDelaySec=1h

That doesn't fix the problem with cron, but it fixes the problem I needed fixing.

title: Cron Daemon Can't Be Coerced Into Restarting on Boot in Debian

title: umask for non-root users not as expected
body:
The default umask for non-root users is generally 0002, 775 for folders and 664 for files in any ubuntu server but it seems to be 0022 in this docker image, I am not sure if this is intended or a issue.

### scenario:
I am using this image to setup a stack for magento. I have installed composer as well as cron inside this image. It's non-production enviroment so I didn't seperate them into own containers to accommodate for limited hardware resources. 

I am using the www-data group as sticky bit to share permissions betwen host and container. The issue arises with files/folders created by cron, composer, php or any other process has umask of 0022, 755 for folders and 644 for files so the files/folders are not writable in host unless sudo, root user or acl is used.

### what I have found:
On default ubuntu installation the umask for non-root user is set by the `pam_umask.so` module. It normally reads from `login.defs` which has a entry called `USERGROUPS_ENAB` which converts umask to 0002 for non-root user which has same same uid and gid. 

The module is generally called from `/etc/pam.d/common-session` , this image seems to be missing the module call in this file as well.

### what I have tried:
1. manually adding `session optional pam_umask.so` at end of  `/etc/pam.d/common-session` and  `/etc/pam.d/common-session-noninteractive` , this does seems to load the umask value from `login.defs`, if I change the value it gets reflected but the non-root user umask due to `USERGROUPS_ENAB` still does not work.

2. manually adding `session optional pam_umask.so` at end of  `/etc/pam.d/common-session` and  `/etc/pam.d/common-session-noninteractive` as well as adding `umask=0002` in www-data `/etc/passwd` gecos field, this works as desired. I can even load the module in `pam.d/cron` and cron tasks umask is 0002 now.

3. lastly, for docker exec command which I use to run composer as www-data, pam_umask module seems to make no difference, for this adding `umask=0002` in www-data user's home `.bashrc` does the job.

### what I want to know:
1. why the `USEGROUPS_ENAB` is failing to set 0002 umask for non-root user www-data, I even created totally new user the umask is still 0022 with `USERGROUPS_ENAB`, adding umask to gecos field works here as well.

2. why is `docker exec -it -u www-data $container_name /bin/bash` not using pam_umask set value, only `.bashrc` works for this or if I manually do `su www-data -s /bin/bash` from root exec pam_umask value is set correctly as well. 

Thank you for reading it, I have done my best to make it brief. I am hoping to get some insights on this.

comments.body:
Unfortunately, this is a known limitations of containers as currently implemented; see https://github.com/moby/moby/issues/19189 and https://github.com/opencontainers/runc/issues/1650 -> https://github.com/opencontainers/runc/pull/2527 (so likely "just" needs the option added in Docker :grimacing:).

I guess your best bet is probably something like setting your command to `bash -c 'umask 0002 && exec ...`:

```console
$ docker run --rm php:8.0-cli php -r 'printf("%04o\n", umask());'
0022
$ docker run --rm php:8.0-cli bash -c 'umask 0002 && exec "$@"' -- php -r 'printf("%04o\n", umask());'
0002
```

Thank you for the issue threads links, they were really useful.

I tried lots of things and currently have found a temporary fix for this image both interactive and non-interactive tasks. I will mention the fix below for any future readers. Also, do keep in mind I am only trying to change umask for non-root users.

### the temporary fix:
1. add `pam_umask` module for `common-session` and `common-session-noninteractive`
2. add `umask=002` in `gecos field / .bashrc` of respective non-root user, since `USERGROUPS_ENAB` is not working at the moment this will allow only non-root users to have separate umask.
3. 1 and 2 above will set umask value for both non-interactive tasks like process/cron as well as commands from interactive shell like bash `docker exec -it -u www-data php bash `
4. since docker exec does not load `.bashrc` so we need to use a wrapper which loads `.bashrc` to fix this `docker exec -it -u www-data php bash -ic "command"`, the important part is the `-i flag` of bash which makes it load the `.bashrc`

### files created from `cron` / `bash` and `docker exec` after using the fixes:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/23445259/112334717-bc53b780-8ce3-11eb-9e28-a0ff2b10121f.png)

### fix from docker side
I am hoping [opencontainers/runc#2527](https://github.com/opencontainers/runc/pull/2527) will fix `docker exec` not loading the `.bashrc` file / provide means to set umask and maybe even fix `USERGROUPS_ENAB` so we don't need to add umas

Glad you got something figured out for what you need.

I'm going to close since there's not anything for us to fix in the PHP image.

@bijay135 Sadly this doesn't work on the php:apache docker image, Apache runs as www-data, but the user account doesn't seem to exist:
```
$ sudo docker exec -it php-apache /bin/bash -c "usermod -c \"umask=002\" www-data && su www-data -c 'echo \"umask 002\" >> /var/www/.bashrc'"
This account is currently not available.
```
Did you have to do anything else to get this www-data user configured?
@tianon I would recommend fixing the part where umask is 0022, should be 0002. Seems like this subtle difference has been the source of countless hours of deployment issues over the years...

I think "This account is currently not available." is probably `su` telling you that the `www-data` user is not one you can "log in" as, but it's hard to say for sure.  The account definitely exists (check `/etc/passwd` and you'll see it, or `getent passwd www-data`).

As for the `umask`, this isn't something we've set explicitly anywhere in this repository or image -- it's being inherited from Docker or other involved software (and it isn't something we can directly "set" on the image anyways -- there's no "UMASK" instruction in a `Dockerfile`, for example).

```console
$ docker pull php:apache
apache: Pulling from library/php
Digest: sha256:67d471f9ce2d1185f0b30f2d89bed811e206462fb2afb0c835932338506e6a19
Status: Image is up to date for php:apache
docker.io/library/php:apache
$ docker run --rm php:apache getent passwd www-data
www-data:x:33:33:www-data:/var/www:/usr/sbin/nologin
$ docker run --rm php:apache grep www-data /etc/passwd
www-data:x:33:33:www-data:/var/www:/usr/sbin/nologin
$ docker run --rm --user www-data php:apache id
uid=33(www-data) gid=33(www-data) groups=33(www-data)
```

> [@bijay135](https://github.com/bijay135) Sadly this doesn't work on the php:apache docker image, Apache runs as www-data, but the user account doesn't seem to exist:
> 
> ```
> $ sudo docker exec -it php-apache /bin/bash -c "usermod -c \"umask=002\" www-data && su www-data -c 'echo \"umask 002\" >> /var/www/.bashrc'"
> This account is currently not available.
> ```
> 
> Did you have to do anything else to get this www-data user configured?

Can't believe this is still a issue after all these years. For your question, try running all commands as below. I pulled php:apache image and tested it, works fine.

```
# Configure www-data user
 && chsh -s /bin/bash www-data && chown :www-data /var/www && chmod g+w /var/www \
 && usermod -c "umask=002" www-data && su www-data -c 'echo "umask 002" >> /var/www/.bashrc'
```

To conclude `www-data` is definitely a user but not a log-innable user. I was wrong about the umask, it is indeed not a php image issue but the "default" on Ubuntu (0022). I was able to get the umask changed to 0002 for Apache which requires modifying the `/etc/apache2/apache2.conf` file and a hard server restart. It may not be the only way, I did not have a chance to try @bijay135's solution above. I wonder if that method persists across reboots?

title: OTRS / Znuny Installation via Debian Package style
body:
As far I understand, the TK Image concept are meant to be pre productive images.
But this OTRS Package is only capable as a preview.
First look is working, but a more scratchy technical review shows problems.

This Issue is not related to the TK Image "itself" - its working;
But the chosen install style won’t become an "easygoing" future Znuny install.

After a short fact finding mission related to a OTRS migration, I discovered some problems with the default Debian Package for otrs2
Errors discovered:
- Default installation path (as recommended by OTRS/Znuny) are changed
above decision is resulting in
- Default rights are not setup properly
- Cronjobs won't run, 
- OTRS Addons cannot be installed (FS right not correct)
- Many Perl Packages are missing; but are available in Debian (wrong / missing dependencies)
- Missing MySQL Settings

I recommend noting this in the Image description to be more accurate and give more/less Power users a hint.

(My plan is to figure out if a OTRS/Znuny installation over a LAMP Image is a working approach; or it's better to go with clean D11 images; and leave a note here)

comments.body:
Thanks for taking the time to share your feedback. Although for what it's worth, we've been providing an OTRS appliance for at least 10 years, using the package from the Debian repos.

This is the first I'm hearing some of these issues, so I've done a bit of reading.

It turns out that some of the "issues" you refer to are the result of conscious Debian decisions to lock things down to harden security. As you are hopefully already aware, security isn't a binary on/off thing and almost all security hardening introduces user limitations. FWIW there is a [Debian bug](https://bugs.debian.org/cgi-bin/bugreport.cgi?bug=475737) which covers the arguments (from both sides). The changes made do limit the ability of OTRS to do things that it wants to do, but it also reduces the chances of something really bad happening if a bad actor gets access to your OTRS/Znuny app.

When we set it up, we run the [`otrs.SetPermissions.pl`](https://github.com/turnkeylinux-apps/otrs/blob/master/conf.d/main#L51-L54) script - which I would have assumed resolved the issues?! Clearly that is not the case - at least for you...

It is also noted in Debian readme (`/usr/share/doc/otrs2/README.Debian`):
```
OTRS package manager:
---------------------

otrs2 includes by default a package manager. This will not work with the Debian
package, because to have it work, we need to relax too many file permissions.

Also have a look here:
    http://bugs.debian.org/cgi-bin/bugreport.cgi?bug=475737

title: Consolidation deletes busy node instead of emptier one
body:
### Description

**Observed Behavior**:
Our clusters scale up every 30 minutes to be able to host all cronjobs. Consolidation usually works as expected and removes the node with fewer/no pods, which is the one that got created to run the cronjobs. However, after the cronjobs run, sometimes a node full of pods is deleted instead of the one empty or with very few pods running. 

At the time most cronjobs finish the cluster can run on fewer nodes. Therefore, the consolidation triggers the deletion of a node, but this less busy node (a couple pods left running maximum) is not picked up for deletion, instead a very busy node with around 50 pods is deleted.

I did not see anything on karpenter debug logs. However, running a node describe on the surviving node I found this:
```
Events:
  Type    Reason             Age                  From       Message
  ----    ------             ----                 ----       -------
  Normal  DisruptionBlocked  42m (x2 over 72m)    karpenter  Cannot disrupt Node: Nominated for a pending pod
```

This is due to cronjobs running every minute on the clusters. So by the time karpenter notices it can remove a node, often times there are new pods that are getting running, which causes this issue.

Deployment spec is as follows
- karpenter's chart is deployed with no custom values affecting its behaviour
- EC2NodeClass has no relevant values that affect consolidation decisions
- NodePools are configured as shown below

```
apiVersion: karpenter.sh/v1beta1
kind: NodePool
metadata:
  name: spot-general-purpose-burstable
spec:
  disruption:
    consolidationPolicy: WhenUnderutilized
    expireAfter: Never
  template:
    spec:
      nodeClassRef:
        name: default
      requirements:
        - key: "node.kubernetes.io/instance-type"
          operator: In
          values: ["t3.large"]
        - key: karpenter.sh/capacity-type
          operator: In
          values: ["spot"]
        - key: kubernetes.io/os	
          operator: In	
          values:	
            - linux	
        - key: kubernetes.io/arch	
          operator: In	
          values:	
            - amd64
      kubelet:
        kubeReserved:
          cpu: 100m
          ephemeral-storage: 1Gi
          memory: 200Mi
        maxPods: 110
        systemReserved:
          cpu: 100m
          ephemeral-storage: 1Gi
          memory: 200Mi
  weight: 50
```

**Expected Behavior**:
I would expect karpenter takes that less busy node for deletion, although it has a pod nominated to run, instead of deleting a far less busy node, to cause the least disruption.

**Versions**:
- Chart Version: 0.37.0
- Kubernetes Version (`kubectl version`): v1.30.0-eks-036c24b

* Please vote on this issue by adding a 👍 [reaction](https://blog.github.com/2016-03-10-add-reactions-to-pull-requests-issues-and-comments/) to the original issue to help the community and maintainers prioritize this request
* Please do not leave "+1" or "me too" comments, they generate extra noise for issue followers and do not help prioritize the request
* If you are interested in working on this issue or have submitted a pull request, please leave a comment

comments.body:
Hey @offzale, we use nomination to be aware of soon-to-schedule or recently scheduled pods. We use this as a way to gate against repeated pod recurring pod disruptions. When a node is nominated, it isn't considered a candidate for consolidation for 10 seconds. So if the pod schedules, we'll consider the next cheapest node to disrupt.  

You can use the pod eviction cost annotation on your pods to weigh away from expensive pods to disrupt: https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/karpenter/blob/main/pkg/utils/disruption/disruption.go#L51

Hi @njtran, thanks for the insights, I understand the issue now. I switched the consolidation policy to `WhenEmpty`, since this happens in an environment where nodes are running with a lot of pods. Then, ideally the node to take down is always the one with fewer pods despite node nominations. Or is there a threshold that if aggregated pod eviction costs for a node goes beyond it, the node will not be a candidate for consolidation?

It could be useful to be able to turn off this consolidation protection for nodes with soon-to-schedule or recently scheduled pods, or be able to skip a consolidation when this happens, and let the next consolidation decide. Since taking down a node with more than 90% of its resources requested when the consolidation policy is `WhenUnderutilized`, instead of another one with a 5% or 10% of resources requested, does not really fit the policy. 

Or maybe a setting for customising how `WhenUnderutilized` behaves, that allow us to set a utilisation threshold. e.g. setting that only nodes with lower requested resources than 75% (this being a customisable value) could be considered underutilised and, therefore, be candidates for scale down. This would avoid, in a customisable way for each use case, to take as candidate a wrong node which is not underutilised at all.

Thoughts?

Thanks so much for reporting this, and sorry it sat for so long without a fix! :(

This was reported on Karpenter v0.37, before v1. A lot has changed since then: the APIs moved to v1, and scheduling, consolidation and node lifecycle have all been reworked across many releases. So this may already behave differently, and an old reproduction is hard for us to act on.

We're closing it to keep the backlog focused. If you still see this on Karpenter v1.14.0 or later, please reopen or file a new issue with reproduction steps (your NodePool/EC2NodeClass, the pod spec, and a few controller log lines help a ton). We'd genuinely love to dig in. :)

This was posted by an AI coding agent on behalf of @AndrewSirenko to help us rein in our backlog. It can be wrong, so feel free to disagree!

title: Native file-based sessions fail with write exception in 1 out of 1000 requests on Debian systems
body:
### Symfony version(s) affected

6.0

### Description

On Debian systems, to prevent session hijacking, the default `session.save_path` is not listable by PHP. This is a sound security feature. In order for this to work :
- session gc must be blocked in the HTTP context (SAPI = CGI or FPM)
- session gc must be handled by an external, privileged process (a root cronjob on Debian)

Thus Debian ships with `session.gc_probability=0` and the proper external gc in `/etc/cron.d/php`. It's been working like a charm for 10+ years (I've traced the presence of this setup since at least Debian 6 / 2011), it still ships that way.

Symfony forces `session.gc_probability=1` which seems to start from a complaint from a filled cache folder (see #10349). It ended with this very strange situation where :
- the default situation with a native file-based session handler on Debian is broken, in a nasty and heisenbuggy way (triggers on 1 out of 1000 queries on average)
- the documentation suggests how to unbreak it (https://symfony.com/doc/current/components/http_foundation/session_configuration.html#configuring-garbage-collection)

Debian-based users thus have a very hard time rediscovering the obscure problem and fixing it.

IMO if Symfony is configured to use the native PHP handler, it should honor the native settings : in this case it is the php.ini's owner responsability to properly configure it, and it turns out Debian ships a well configured situation. A value of `session.gc_probability=1` can't be forced by ignoring the whereabouts of the session handler, because a value of 0 can be sound and right.

I think the intention was right (never ship a configuration which let a session storage endlessly fills up), but the fix is wrong.

I would like to request to at least not break Debian native file-based session handler by default.


### How to reproduce

Grab a Debian OS (>= 6), install your preferred runtime (php-cgi | php-fpm | libapache2-mod-php), and have a simple script like :
```
<?php
ini_set('session.gc_probability', 1);
session_start();
$_SESSION['foo']='bar';
```

Then make a few thousand requests on this script :
```
ab -c1 -n5000 localhost/testsess.php
```

And find in your error.log a rare occurence of :
```
PHP Notice:  session_start(): ps_files_cleanup_dir: opendir(/var/lib/php/sessions) failed: Permission denied (13) in /var/www/default/testsess.php on line 3
```


### Possible Solution

Only force `session.gc_probability=1` when using a non-native session handler, where Symfony and its configuration are really in charge of the sessions.


### Additional Context

_No response_

2. Use a custom session directory

https://symfony.com/doc/current/session.html#configuring-garbage-collection

comments.body:
@chlarsen This is because snapshots with a prefix aren't considered for deleting unless you're searching for them.

So the correct command would be:

```
zfsnap destroy -rnv -p 'server-hourly- server-daily- server-weekly- server-monthly-' 
```

This behavior, to a certain extent, doesn't make a whole lot of sense, as it treats a lack of a prefix as a prefix. And at very least, the documentation should be more clear. I'll take a look how zfsnap 1.x behaved and see if this is a change in behavior.

---Alex

title: Deploy Wikibase Quality Constraints
body:
- https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/Extension:WikibaseQualityConstraints
- https://github.com/wikimedia/mediawiki-extensions-WikibaseQualityConstraints/blob/master/README.md

## Findings (2026-10-23, local test)

Tested `REL1_46` (`d470fc95`) on the `ghcr.io/femiwiki/femiwiki:latest` image (MW 1.46.2) with the dev `compose.yaml`, the extension bind-mounted and loaded from `Hotfix.php`. Constraint checks work: violations come back from `action=wbcheckconstraints` and show as icons next to statements for logged-in users.

### Why the 2020 attempt showed nothing

- **No "constraints" section on property pages.** That section is not part of the extension. Wikidata gets it from `$wgWBRepoSettings['statementSections']['property']` plus the message `wikibase-statementsection-constraints`, which lives in WikimediaMessages. With the config below the section appears; the heading needs `MediaWiki:Wikibase-statementsection-constraints` on the wiki.
- **No checks.** `ImportConstraintEntities` imports the constraint vocabulary (labels only, statements cleared). It adds no constraint to any property. Checks only run for properties that carry "property constraint" statements, and `wbqc_constraints` stays empty until those exist and `ImportConstraintStatements` or the update job reads them. The 2020 steps above have no step that adds constraint statements.
- The extension never blocks an edit. It only reports violations (statement icons, `Special:ConstraintReport`, the API).

### Problems the import script hits on Femiwiki

- **It stops on a Korean wiki when an entity already exists.** `ConstraintScopeId` and `ConstraintEntityTypesId` both default to `P4680`, so the second import fails on duplicate labels. The script recovers from that only by matching the English error text, and Femiwiki's content language is Korean, so it throws and prints no config. Workaround: set `ConstraintEntityTypesId` to a placeholder before the import and to the same ID as `ConstraintScopeId` after.
- **It does not check the HTTP response.** One Wikimedia error page in the middle of the 67 fetches stopped the run locally after part of the entities were created, again without printing config. Recovery is to read the mapping back from the importer's edit summaries (`imported from [[wikidata:…]]`).
- **`P31`/`P279` must not be imported.** Femiwiki already has "다음 종류에 속함" (`P1`) and "다음의 하위 개념임" (`P36`), and Femiwiki's `P31` is an unrelated property. Set `InstanceOfId`/`SubclassOfId` before the import and the script skips them.
- Local only: `MEDIAWIKI_DEBUG_MODE` loads `DevelopmentSettings.php`, which sets `$wgMaxArticleSize = 20`, too small for the imported entities. Production uses the default 2048.

The import creates 67 entities (19 properties, 48 items) with Wikidata's labels in every language, Korean included. Edits are flagged bot, and `$wgRCFeeds['discord']` has `omit_bots`.

### Jobs, cron, SPARQL

- **No new cron.** Editing a property's constraint statements queues `constraintsTableUpdate`, which the existing every-minute `run-jobs` cron runs (verified locally). Creating a property with constraints in the same edit does not queue it (the hook only handles updates); `ImportConstraintStatements` covers those, and later edits catch up.
- `CheckConstraintsJob` (`WBQualityConstraintsEnableConstraintsCheckJobs`) is off by default and only pre-fills the result cache. Results are cached in the WAN cache for a day and cleared on purge.
- **No SPARQL endpoint** means:
  - *Distinct values* (Unique value) always returns `todo` and shows nothing.
  - *Format* returns `todo` unless the exact pattern is in `$wgWBQualityConstraintsFormatCheckerKnownGoodRegexPatterns` (then PHP runs it; verified) or Shellbox is set up. A new regex then needs a config deploy.
  - *Type* and *Value type* walk the class tree in PHP up to `WBQualityConstraintsTypeCheckMaxEntities` (1000). That is enough for ~450 items; past the limit they return false without SPARQL.
  - All other types run in PHP.

Hello NLnetLabs Team,
Im reaching out to you as you're the last instance.
I have NSD servres running as one primary and multiple secondary servers pointing to the same primary as for the source of truth. Primary and Secondary NSD servers don't know anything about each other.
Primary NSD configured to allow XFR queries to come from the subnets of Secondary NSD hosts.
Running nsd-control transfer on Secondary hosts is used to fetch the zones configured in nsd.conf file at secondary instance bootstrap. The same cmd is configured as Cron job and runs every 5min. This way I know that the zone changes I make on the primary host will appear on secondary in not more than 5min.
The reason I don't have notify section configured on the primary host is that secondary hosts are cloud vms and can be replaced by the cloud for any reason and at any time. This makes it impossible to preconfigure Primary NSD with ip addresses of any secondary servers.

Recently the sync between primary and the secondary hosts didn't work.
Quick check on secondary hosts with cmd "nsd-control zonestatus" showed that of the zones has its state as "refreshing".
I tried to run nsd-control transfer in my terminal but that didn't change anything, then I ran "nsd-control force_transfer" 
which made a zone transfer ignoring Serial field of SOA reacord of all zones and the issue was fixed.
Repeating nsd-control zonestatus was showing all zones "status: ok".
After checking the logs I saw some weird stuff:
nsd.log:
_[timestamp] nsd[475]: error: xfrd: failed writing tcp Operation now in progress

## Proposal summary

We propose adding package management to CUE, using an approach analogous to Go using Minimum Version Selection and semantic versioning. The changes are limited to `cmd/cue` and the [`cue/load`](https://pkg.go.dev/cuelang.org/go@master/cue/load) package, and hence have no bearing on CUE the language. 

As an interim measure, we propose using [proxy.golang.org](https://proxy.golang.org/) as a module mirror, and the checksum database [sum.golang.org](https://sum.golang.org) for authentication, until such time as the CUE project can host such services itself. Use of these services will be enabled by default for `cmd/cue` and `cue/load`, but entirely configurable, just like `cmd/go`.

The proposed approach is broadly identical to the approach followed by Go modules. Indeed this proposal borrows heavily from [Russ Cox's blog posts introducing `vgo`](https://research.swtch.com/vgo), the [core Go modules documentation](https://golang.org/ref/mod), and interactions with Bryan Mills and Jay Conrod from the Go team. 

For those who might be less familiar with Go, in particular Go modules, for the more significant parts of this proposal the relevant parts of the Go module reference have been copied and adapted for the CUE context to save jumping between multiple documents. For less significant parts of the proposal, or those for where the concept is truly identical between both approaches, then we generally choose to link to the relevant Go documentation.

## I understand Go modules; what's the TL;DR?
Here is an abridged version for those who have a working knowledge of Go modules, presented from the user perspective with various implementation considerations thrown in where relevant. 

What will be different?

* We will rename the current `cue get go`  to `cue import go` - see #646.
* The root of a CUE module is identified by a `cue.mod` directory; the root of a Go module is identified by a `go.mod` file.
* For a CUE module to be shareable (i.e. act as a dependency for another module), it will also need to include a `go.mod` file that mirrors the `cue.mod/module.cue` file.
* In CUE the main module can be anonymous (a `cue.mod` directory without a `module.cue` file); in Go this is not possible. 
* In Go we speak of building a package, whereas in CUE we speak of evaluating a package, or more precisely an instance (because a package can have multiple instances).
* CUE modules do not have to deal with a pre-module legacy (read: a GOPATH equivalent).
* CUE modules declare the module path (optional in CUE), requirements, retractions etc in `cue.mod/module.cue`; this file is semantically equivalent to `go.mod`, with all directives supported albeit via a different syntax.
* CUE modules will use `cue.mod/sum.cue` as its equivalent of `go.sum`, but in a CUE format (for consistency with `cue.mod/module.cue`).
* The vendor directory will be `cue.mod/pkg`, as it is today.
* CUE uses the `cue/load` package for loading CUE instances. Go has no equivalent, and instead relies on `golang.org/x/tools/go/packages` to wrap `cmd/go`. Working with CUE modules therefore does not require the user to have `cmd/cue` installed.
* The `cue/load.Config` configuration type is extended with the necessary fields for controlling module resolution and loading behaviour; these are essentially the backends to the frontend flags and environment variables available in `cmd/cue`.
* Vanity import paths will be supported through `cue-import` `<meta>` HTML tags with a fallback to `go-import`.
* There is support for CUE and Go modules coexisting at the same module path within the same source code repository. See "Go modules and CUE modules coexisting" for mod .


What is the same?

* The definition of a main module is identical in CUE: the main module is the module containing the directory where the loader is invoked

I encountered the same issue (service failing with exit-code, status=1/FAILURE). Ubuntu 22.04. TG Proxy Go.

It turns out the binary works fine, but the systemd service configuration prevents it from writing to the log files due to `DynamicUser=true`.

Here is how to fix it:

1. Verify the binary works manually
Run this command in your terminal to confirm the config is actually correct:
``` Bash
/opt/hiddify-manager/other/telegram/tgo/mtg run /opt/hiddify-manager/other/telegram/tgo/mtg.toml
```
If this runs successfully (you see logs and no immediate crash), proceed to step 2.

2. Fix the Systemd Service permissions
The service fails because the dynamic user cannot access the log directory.

Open the service file:
```Bash
nano /etc/systemd/system/mtproxy.service
```
Find the `[Service]` section. You need to remove `DynamicUser=true` and add `User=root`.

It should look like this:
``` Ini, TOML
[Service]
ExecStart=/opt/hiddify-manager/other/telegram/tgo/mtg run /opt/hiddify-manager/other/telegram/tgo/mtg.toml
Restart=always
RestartSec=3
# DynamicUser=true  <-- DELETE OR COMMENT THIS OUT
User=root           <-- ADD THIS
AmbientCapabilities=CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE
StandardOutput=file:/opt/hiddify-manager/log/system/telegram.out.log
StandardError=file:/opt/hiddify-manager/log/system/telegram.err.log
```
3. Apply changes and restart
``` Bash
systemctl daemon-reload
systemctl restart mtproxy
systemctl status mtproxy
```
This fixed the issue for me instantly.

title: Not all instances are updated via update-lgsm on a multi instance game server
body:
## User Story

As a multi instance game server owner, I want manage LinuxGSM and game server updates as easy as possible.
Now, I have problems, because not all the instances are updated with the `update-lgsm` command started from the first instance.

## Basic info

* **Distro:** [Debian 10]
* **Game:** [Counter-Strike: Global Offensive]
* **Command:** [update-lgsm]
* **LinuxGSM version:** [v20.2.0]

## Further Information

I setup my crons like this:
```
# Server #1
@reboot su - csgoserver -c '/home/csgoserver/csgoserver monitor' > /dev/null 2>&1
35 3 * * * su - csgoserver -c '/home/csgoserver/csgoserver update' > /dev/null 2>&1
0 0 * * 0 su - csgoserver -c '/home/csgoserver/csgoserver update-functions' > /dev/null 2>&1

# Server #2
@reboot su - csgoserver -c '/home/csgoserver/csgoserver-2 monitor' > /dev/null 2>&1
34 3 * * * su - csgoserver -c '/home/csgoserver/csgoserver-2 stop' > /dev/null 2>&1
40 3 * * * su - csgoserver -c '/home/csgoserver/csgoserver-2 start' > /dev/null 2>&1

# Server #3
@reboot su - csgoserver -c '/home/csgoserver/csgoserver-3 monitor' > /dev/null 2>&1
34 3 * * * su - csgoserver -c '/home/csgoserver/csgoserver-3 stop' > /dev/null 2>&1
40 3 * * * su - csgoserver -c '/home/csgoserver/csgoserver-3 start' > /dev/null 2>&1
```

The `update` is updating game server files under every instance (because every instance is using the same files), but `update-functions` is only updating the first `csgoserver` instance, not `csgoserver-2` and `csgoserver-3`.

And I had strange problems because of this. Every instance is using different LinuxGSM versions:
`./csgoserver details` (LinuxGSM version: **v20.2.0**)
`./csgoserver-2 details` (LinuxGSM version: **v19.9.0**)
`./csgoserver-3 details` (LinuxGSM version: **v19.9.0**)

## To Reproduce

Steps to reproduce the behaviour:
1. have multi instance game servers
2. use `update-functions` only on the first instance
3. other instances will stay on an older LinuxGSM version
4. it can cause errors, like this:
```
csgoserver@debian:~$ ./csgoserver start
[ INFO ] Starting csgoserver: Check IP: x.x.x.x
[  OK  ] Starting csgoserver: SERVERNAME
csgoserver@debian:~$ ./csgoserver-2 start
mkdir: cannot create directory ‘’: No such file or directory
[ INFO ] Starting csgoserver-2: Check IP: x.x.x.x
[ .... ] Starting csgoserver-2: SERVERNAME/home/csgoserver/lgsm/functions/command_start.sh: line 65: /csgoserver-2.lock: Permission denied
/home/csgoserver/lgsm/functions/command_start.sh: line 73: /csgoserver-2-laststart.lock: Permission denied
[  OK  ] Starting csgoserver-2: SERVERNAME
csgoserver@debian:~$ ./csgoserver-3 start
mkdir: cannot create directory ‘’: No such file or directory
[ INFO ] Starting csgoserver-3: Check IP: x.x.x.x
[ .... ] Starting csgoserver-3: SERVERNAME/home/csgoserver/lgsm/functions/command_start.sh: line 65: /csgoserver-3.lock: Permission denied
/home/csgoserver/lgsm/functions/command_start.sh: line 73: /csgoserver-3-laststart.lock: Permission denied
[  OK  ] Starting csgoserver-3: SERVERNAME
```

`./csgoserver start` is working fine, because it's using the up-to-date version of LinuxGSM. Others give errors because the new LinuxGSM version has some breaking changes since the `v19.9.0`, and the last two instances are using that.

You have to run `update-functions` on every instance, because versions differences can cause problems.

## Expected behaviour

Update every instance with `update-functions` started on any instance as `update` works with game server files.

comments.body: So potential idea for this is to have the lgsm version located in both ./gameserver and in core_functions. When ./gameserver does anything it will compare these versions. If they do not match the update-lgsm will run to sync up versions to prevent a module an update mismatch

~Closed
feature in version 20.3.0 included

Hi @AndrePhP-tech 

Thanks for this!

> In Plesk I am able to: (i) run a command, (ii) fetch a URL, and (iii) run a PHP script.

It should be the option 2, " fetch a URL"


> When I 'run a PHP script' this is the output:
> Could not open input file: https://mywebsite.co.uk/asset/cron/24h/Birthday/?secret_word=*******

These cron jobs shouldn't be run by PHP, but by a GET request. More information here: https://www.ph7cms.com/doc/en/cron


> When I 'fetch a URL' this is the output:
> Status: 403
> Output:
> <title>403 Forbidden</title>

**Apparently, something from your website (maybe the `.htaccess`...) blocks cURL to run the cron on your website, which gives back the 403 error.** Usually, for security reasons.

Can you ask your server to investigate this? And give them all the information you can find on this page?

**A very similar issue was: https://github.com/pH7Software/pH7-Social-Dating-CMS/issues/182 Maybe it could help you or your web host...**


*Finally, some URLs that might be useful for you :)*
- https://www.ph7cms.com/doc/en/cron
- https://www.ph7cms.com/doc/en/cron-list
- https://github.com/pH7Software/pH7-Social-Dating-CMS/issues/233#issuecomment-404476443
- https://github.com/pH7Software/pH7-Social-Dating-CMS/issues/182

It should be something like below. Hopefully, this will help you or your web host:

---
crontab -e
```
0 0 * * *  GET "https://mywebsite.co.uk/asset/cron/24h/Birthday?secret_word=REPLACE_BY_YOUR_SECRET_WORD"
```

comments.body: 你的问题我也遇到了，我在https://github.com/coolsnowwolf/lede/issues/12305时遇到的是wan口有问题，后来发现lan口也有问题，就是无法识别网卡。前两天我又编译了一次，问题多出了一个和你一样的，wifi只有2.4g，5g的无线接口都没了。提了issue但估计没看就close了
我也遇到了一样的问题。

已核对该日志：AX6S 的两个关键故障分别是 PCIe 报 `missing hifsys node` 导致 5 GHz 无线 PCIe 设备未探测，以及 MT7531 使用错误 MDIO 地址导致交换机探测失败，所以会同时表现为只有 2.4 GHz、网口无法访问路由器管理地址。当前 master 已包含 commit `e66721c4e321e1a71702bbe1afe10b322fa97b0f`（`mediatek: fix Redmi AX6S hardware initialization`）：将交换机地址修正为 `<31>`，并补齐两路无线 nvmem 校准区域，配合现有 PCIe hifsys 支持。该 issue 的修复已在当前代码中，关闭。

title: Using dokku-acl with dokku-letsencrypt breaks auto-renewal
body:
We use `dokku-acl` together with the [`dokku-letsencrypt`](https://github.com/dokku/dokku-letsencrypt) plugin. For auto-renewal of certificates, the plugin creates a cronjob for the dokku-User:

```
@daily /var/lib/dokku/plugins/available/letsencrypt/cron-job
```

which in turn executes

```
dokku letsencrypt:auto-renew &>> /var/log/dokku/letsencrypt.log
```

which fails on our hosts:

```
User default does not have permissions to run letsencrypt:auto-renew
Access denied
```

What would be the best way to fix this issue? I thought about some ways, but I didn't find one which works well...

1. We've set `export DOKKU_SUPER_USER=dokku`. So if the cronjob would export `NAME` it should work, right?
2. We could add `letsencrypt:auto-renew` to `DOKKU_ACL_USER_COMMANDS`. But since `letsencrypt:auto-renew` calls `letsencrypt` and `certs:add`, we would need to whitelist those functions for all apps as well, which is undesirable.

comments.body:
Sorry for getting to this so late:

- Can you turn on events via `dokku events:on`, trigger the cronjob - don't run letsencrypt directly! - and show the output of `/var/log/dokku/events.log`? It should contain the user that the cronjob is running as. It's possible it is running as root or something.

Thanks for your reply!

I did the following:
- enabled dokku events
- edited dokku's crontab to run the letsencrypt cron-job in the next minute

`/var/log/dokku/events.log`:
```
Dec  7 11:01:01 app2 dokku[21011]: INVOKED: user-auth(  default letsencrypt:auto-renew ) NAME= FINGERPRINT=
Dec  7 11:01:02 app2 dokku[21647]: INVOKED: user-auth(  default letsencrypt zweitag-shoebox ) NAME= FINGERPRINT=
```

`/var/log/dokku/letsencrypt.log`:
```
=====> Auto-renewing all apps...
-----> test-app needs renewal
User default does not have permissions to run letsencrypt
Access denied
```
Where is the crontab file specified?

I edited the crontab w ith `sudo crontab -u dokku -l` to look like this:

```
# @daily /var/lib/dokku/plugins/available/letsencrypt/cron-job
00 09 * * * /var/lib/dokku/plugins/available/letsencrypt/cron-job
```

The default username for dokku is [`default`](https://github.com/dokku/dokku/blob/99fcd613fefe3a97755391a8c9ee19d80838bbaa/plugins/common/functions#L711). This will be used if the `NAME` environment variable isn't set. We don't default that to `dokku` but maybe we should?

If we did, that wouldn't break anything in dokku core, and the acl plugin would continue working as expected (the logged in `dokku` would work), just we would enable background jobs to work.

Anyone have any thoughts on this?

I think that makes sense, I’d appreciate the rename of the default Dokku’s username to `dokku`.

I found this issue a few days ago when I was investigating the difficulties of allowing my friend to host his website on my server. I spent some time testing if the reported issue is still a problem nowadays, and came up to the conclusion that as long as your SSH key is called `default`, and your super-admin username is set to `default`, you’ll be able to renew LE certificates from `cron`, access all commands as expected when you have direct access to the server’s SSH and when interacting with Dokku remotely.

But definitely renaming the user from `default` to `dokku` would have felt cleaner.
(Alternatively – or in addition – it would’ve been nice to be able to specify multiple super-admin accounts – but perhaps that’s a different issue altogether)

title: Stop Xeoma from auto-updating
body:
What's the best way to disable the hourly CRON job that updates Xeoma?

When you run this image specifying a specific version of Xeoma using environment variables, it starts up with the desired version.  At some point, however, Xeoma gets updated to the latest version regardless of what is specified in the VERSION setting.  This is undesirable because if the user's license doesn't cover the very latest version then Xeoma will stop working (switches to supporting 0 devices).  The update occurs even if updating is disabled in the Xeoma GUI.

Ideally it wouldn't try to update if the user has specified anything other than "latest" for VERSION.

title: Unclear documentation about different "run modes" of acme.sh (with / without config files)
body:
From what I understand acme.sh seems to have at least two **different run modes** that seem to be:
* the first run mode **expects** some environment variables to be set and **writes** config files, but does **not read** config files
* the second run mode **reads config files** - but it is not clear if it ignores environment variables.

This is a strange behaviour for a shell script and leads to several problems - e.g. what do I need to do if I want to move / reinstall acme.sh on a new machine? Can I just backup the config files? Also it is not clear what happens with env vars when acme.sh is run a second time. And what about cron? 

It seems like you want to keep the configuration files "private", like in a private java class - I do not think this is a good idea, as it makes handling of acme.sh complicated. Also there is a very well established way of doing things in bash scripts regarding config files and environment variables - usually environment variables **override**  configuration values found in a config file - it is not clear how acme.sh handles this.

It would be very helpful to have more documentation about the relation of acme.sh config files / env vars / "run modes" as a first help. In the long term it seems like that handling should be adopted to the way this might be expected on a unix system, like described above. Thank you!

comments.body:
sorry about missing doc.

There are a few rules:

1.  acme.sh  respects environment variables first.  acme.sh assumes a default value for each variables, but if you defined a environment variable with the same name, we will use the environment variable instead.
Take the "ACCOUNT_CONF_PATH" variable as an example.
And you can check the `_initpath()` function for more details.
2. If you defined a environment variable rather than the default value,  the variable will be remembered in the config file, and will be reused next time.
3. If you define a new value for the environment variable for the second time,  usually, the old value will be overwritten in the config file.


Yes, acme.sh has 2 running modes:
1. The user mode:   acme.sh is invoked by the user, with command parameters to issue cert or revoke or etc.
2. The cron mode:  acme.sh is running as a cron job, in which, acme.sh expects to load all the variable from the config file(the account conf or the domain conf).

BTW,
We encourage users to use acme.sh by command parameters,  rather than editing the config files directly.
That's why we don't have doc about the config files.

If you need any more info,  I can add more command parameters for you to use, if reasonable.

Thanks.

The problem with env vars is that it is not possible to define multiple values - e.g. it is not possible to define multiple target servers for the ssh deploy command. Please see https://github.com/Neilpang/acme.sh/issues/1714 and https://github.com/Neilpang/acme.sh/issues/1406
Closing as stale: no activity for over 18 months. If this still applies on the current release, please open a new issue with the `--debug 2` log.

title: Archiving via cron with custom php executable and php.ini file
body:
There are several issues for me with the archiving via cron when I have a custom php executable and a custom php.ini file. 

First of all the console uses hardcoded the php executable found in the PATH variable through the shebang in the console script. I can workaround this with the following call:

hash /usr/local/software/php/5.5.15/bin/php php && /usr/local/software/php/5.5.15/bin/php -c .../my_custom_php.ini .../piwik/console core:archive ...
So instead of using the system wide php binary the same php executable is used which is used to invoke the console (as long as the path to the custom php executable is the same as the one set with "hash /usr/local/software/php/5.5.15/bin/php php") including all passed parameters like a custom .ini file. 

But the parameter "-c" is not passed to the forked php process done by CLI archiving. I think this should be done by the CliPhp class which returns the path to the PHP binary. Arguments for the php executable should be added there.

I have this problem as the json extension is not installed system wide but only through my custom ini file which results in an error as piwik has the wrong ini file.

I hope the problem description is understandable.

comments.body: Setting "export PHP_INI_SCAN_DIR=/var/www/fcgi-bin.d/tegut.com-213_174_33_110-80/" before calling the archiving seems to help neither.

We're most likely taking the PPH version defined in the constant `PHP_BINARY`. This should be the PHP binary path of the current script execution. The `-c` option is a good point, we should actually indeed forward this option, maybe not all options though (I'm not sure we'd probably just have to read over several options) :+1:

Related to #9258 - forwarding parameters to CLI scripts
and maybe also related to https://github.com/piwik/piwik/issues/8771
Duplicate of #5328

title: Memories app causes Nextcloud cron to use excessive amount of resources (oc_filecache queries)
body:
### Describe the bug

I noticed that my Nextcloud server uses a lot of CPU periodically, and the timing correlates with running the Nextcloud cron task.

I enabled logging all queries on my PostgreSQL instance and noticed that Nextcloud cron task runs a lot of queries against `oc_filecache` table:
```
2024-10-15 18:50:31.782 UTC [40] LOG:  execute <unnamed>: SELECT "filecache"."fileid", "storage", "path", "path_hash", "filecache"."parent", "filecache"."name", "mimetype", "mimepart", "size", "mtime", "storage_mtime", "encrypted", "etag", "filecache"."permissions", "checksum", "unencrypted_size", "metadata_etag", "creation_time", "upload_time", "meta"."json" AS "meta_json", "meta"."sync_token" AS "meta_sync_token" FROM "oc_filecache" "filecache" LEFT JOIN "oc_filecache_extended" "fe" ON "filecache"."fileid" = "fe"."fileid" LEFT JOIN "oc_files_metadata" "meta" ON "filecache"."fileid" = "meta"."file_id" WHERE "filecache"."parent" = $1 ORDER BY "name" ASC
```

This results in a high CPU activity on both Nextcloud and the database container (PostgreSQL 16). 

My instance is not very large, about 400K files in total, images make up a fraction of that (10-25K probably). 
I've already truncated the `oc_filecache` table, reindexed the table in Postgres, and done a full rescan via `occ`, but that did not improve the situation.

I've done all the optimizations mentioned in the issue template, even before using Memories.
Transcoding is enabled. Recognize is disabled.

After disabling Memories app within Nextcloud, the cron task uses a reasonable amount of CPU.

A quick code search over this repo suggests use of the filecache table so I suspect that the load is caused by the Memories app. I've seen similar reports of other people struggling with similar issues on the filecache table, but I did not notice any relations to a specific app like Memories.

I tried searching existing issues for similar topics but could not find one. 

### Steps To Reproduce

I don't have the time to test this out on a fully clean Nextcloud system, but I reckon it can be tested like this:
1. set up a clean Nextcloud instance (Docker, Postgres)
2. install and enable Memories
3. create a large number of files (1+ million to be safe), a good chunk of them images/videos
4. set Nextcloud cron task to be run every 5 minutes
5. observe CPU and container resource usage over time

### Platform

```markdown
Platform:
Nextcloud Hub 8 (29.0.7) (official Docker image)
Memories 7.4.1
PostgreSQL 16 (official Docker image)
```


### Screenshots

Attached is the CPU usage graph of my server, with Memories app enabled and disabled.

![Screenshot from 2024-10-16 19-37-59](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/40d70e5e-d731-41e6-8d12-679b63e3b051)

I have not had this run for a very long time, but the effect is noticeable already.

### Additional context

No relevant errors in Nextcloud logs.

Today the problem happened again. The search bar doesn't work, because the required file "search_list.json" is not available in the production container.

The logs in Rancher show that cron jobs are run, for example gen_search_list.sh and course_reminders.sh.
The actual emails sent also show that the course reminders job did run. So some cron jobs are working?

But still the required json file, which is generated by gen_search_list.sh is not available.

I have 3 detailed screenshot available and will send them to Dalibor per email. Since they are taken from the Rachner environment I'll not post them here.

Edit/update: Since I executed the job manually from the shell, it works again (for now).

Addition: The rancher logs do show an error, 2 minutes after the cron job did run (at 10:17:21) Message: Unable to retrieve some image pull secrets; attempting to pull the image may not succeed.
@dpancic Can you help to solve this?

According to line 39 in [GenSearchListCommand.php](https://github.com/acdh-oeaw/dhcr-main/blob/prod/src/Command/GenSearchListCommand.php) cronjob named dhcr-gen-search-list should create search_list.json in /webroot directory. The cronjob is doing it correctly. 

The app cannot reach and use  search_list.json because it is not located in the app container. 
The cronjob is executed in a separate container and does not have shared directories with the app.

The problem can be solved by creating PVC that will be shared between the cronjob and the container with the app.
The GenSearchListCommand.php should be reconfigured to store search_list.json in the mounted (shared) directory (for example /cronjob-output, and the app should be reconfigured to expect search_list.json in /cronjob-output directory.

The PVC named cronjob-output is created and mounted in the app and in all cronjob containers as /cronjob-output. 

@patrickakk please adjust the GenSearchListCommand.php and the app accordingly.

The error related to Gitlab secrets is false warning and unrelated to our deployment. We are not using Gitlab with this app. It can be ignored.

In that case all the paths are still inside the Git repo. That makes it easier compatible between (local) development and the deployment.

I successfully followed the instructions in this repository to set up a Docker borgmatic set up to back up files from a source on the Docker *host* (e.g. `/path/to/files`) to a repository also on the host (e.g. `/path/to/repo`).

What I want is the ability to *at least* read this repository from the Docker *host*, and ideally read and write access.

One thing I tried is use the `--user` argument with user and group IDs (e.g. 123:456) from the Docker host like this when creating and running this container: `docker run --user 123:456 [other arguments go here...]` However, this fails because apparently crontab inside the container "requires suid privileges".

title: Audit results
body:
I'll put small things that I notice doing my audit of this here, which aren't big/important enough to get their own issue.

 - [x] `self_check_dns.yml`: maybe use the dig lookup plugin instead of a command, and if you use a command, use a command and not a shell.
 - [ ] There are a lot of set_fact tasks, that don't depend on anything that is only available at runtime, moving those into defaults or vars (depending on what they are exactly) would make sense IMO.
 - [x] There should not be a default UID/GID for the matrix user (if this is even a user that should exist, having dedicated users for components would also be a possibility). When creating a user using ansible it has the UID/GID in the result and then you can use that.
 - [ ] The whole letsencrypt business is a bit weird, I really don't like certbot. Have you thought about maybe using dehydrated here? I think it integrates with ansible+containers a lot better than certbot
 - [ ] `setup/ssl/setup_ssl_self_signed_obtain_for_domain.yml`:  You could generate the ssl cert manually only on hosts which don't provide up to date pyopenssl and do the proper way on other hosts
 - [x] periodic nginx restarts could be done with the crontab module instead of templating a cron.d file
 - [x] the start tasks thingy could (and should) be replaced with a loop. also, daemon_reload is not needed there. We also don't need daemon_reload in a lot of other cases, that should be handled with a handler and not a task.
 - [x] going from yaml truth values to json truth values via "true if var else false" is ugly, you can use the |to_json filter for that
 - [ ] if the docker_container module of ansible is used for launching the containers, the env file templates are unnecessary, the vars can just be taken from vars directly

If we install nginx anyway, we might as well just install it before generating the certificates and just enable the sites needing those certs after certs where generated. Alternatively, dehydrated supports dns-01, o

Thank you again for this audit, it was genuinely useful back in 2019 and several items were fixed directly because of it (the DNS self-check, the to_json cleanup, and others checked off above).

Closing it now because the playbook it audited no longer exists in that form, and every remaining unchecked item has been resolved or made moot by later architecture changes:

- The set_fact / vars containment concern: the monolithic role was long ago split into dedicated per-component roles (`roles/custom/matrix-*`), which is exactly the containment you were arguing for.
- certbot / dehydrated and the self-signed SSL generation: the playbook migrated to Traefik as the default reverse proxy, which handles ACME natively. certbot, matrix-nginx-proxy, and all the `setup_ssl_*` task files are gone.
- The start.yml loop and daemon_reload handling: service startup is now managed by the extracted [systemd_service_manager](https://github.com/devture/com.devture.ansible.role.systemd_service_manager) role.
- The default UID/GID for the matrix user: `matrix_user_uid` and `matrix_user_gid` now default to null and are auto-detected after user creation.
- env-file templates vs the docker_container module: running containers via systemd units invoking `docker run` remains a deliberate design choice, so this one we are consciously not pursuing.

If anyone spots a code-quality issue in the current playbook, a fresh, focused issue (or PR) is very welcome.

title: [Bug]: Trusted Server Stuck at Yellow/Orange
body:
### ⚠️ This issue respects the following points: ⚠️

- [X] This is a **bug**, not a question or a configuration/webserver/proxy issue.
- [X] This issue is **not** already reported on [Github](https://github.com/nextcloud/server/issues?q=is%3Aopen+is%3Aissue+label%3Abug) OR [Nextcloud Community Forum](https://help.nextcloud.com/) _(I've searched it)_.
- [X] Nextcloud Server **is** up to date. See [Maintenance and Release Schedule](https://github.com/nextcloud/server/wiki/Maintenance-and-Release-Schedule) for supported versions.
- [X] I agree to follow Nextcloud's [Code of Conduct](https://nextcloud.com/contribute/code-of-conduct/).

### Bug description

In the Federation app, the pairing for Trusted Servers can be flaky.
This is because the way in which `shared_secret` is established is prone to race conditions leading to deadlocks.

There have been numerous reports of people being stuck in the orange state over the years:

- https://help.nextcloud.com/t/federated-trusted-servers-all-on-yellow-not-green/15152
- https://help.nextcloud.com/t/federation-cannot-add-trusted-server/8905
- https://github.com/nextcloud/server/issues/22510

I had the same issue today and investigated a bit. First, I will describe how the pairing flow works. Next, I will describe a situation where it can get stuck in the yellow state, and how to work around it. Finally, I'll suggest possible improvements.

I apologise in advance for the huge information dump. :grimacing: 

## How the Pairing Works

The happy path is as follows:

1. Server A adds Server B as a trusted server, and vice versa.
  a. This calls [`addServer`](https://github.com/nextcloud/server/blob/daf3b29572921562abcb700052c1de19fdd2fe4e/apps/federation/lib/TrustedServers.php#L86) which (1) generates a random token, and (2) adds a job to execute `RequestSharedSecret`.
  b. When people [on the forum recommend](https://help.nextcloud.com/t/federated-trusted-servers-all-on-yellow-not-green/15152/22) to run `php cron.php`, this just causes the background job to be executed immediately, rather than waiting for the next normal cron to run.
  
At this point, A's admin settings are yellow 🟡 and A's database looks like this (`shared_secret` and `sync_token` are both NULL):

```
MariaDB [nextcloud]> select * from oc_trusted_servers;
+----+-----------------------------+------------------------------------------+------------------+----------------------------------+--------+-----------------------------+
| id | url                         | url_hash                                 | token            | shared_secret                    | status | sync_token                  |
+----+-----------------------------+------------------------------------------+------------------+----------------------------------+--------+-----------------------------+
| 17 | https://cloud-b.example.com | aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa | tttttttttttttttt | NULL                             |      2 | NULL                        |
+----+-----------------------------+------------------------------------------+------------------+----------------------------------+--------+-----------------------------+
```
  
2. Cloud A's `RequestSharedSecret` [does a](https://github.com/nextcloud/server/blob/daf3b29572921562abcb700052c1de19fdd2fe4e/apps/federation/lib/BackgroundJob/RequestSharedSecret.php#L131) `POST https://cloud-a.example.com/ocs/v2.php/apps/federation/api/v1/request-shared-secret` with body `{token: aaa}`. I.e. Cloud A sends its token to Cloud B.
3. Cloud B receives it, and **if** Cloud A's token is larger than B's token (happy path, see more below!!), B [creates a job](https://github.com/nextcloud/server/blob/daf3b29572921562abcb700052c1de19fdd2fe4e/apps/federation/lib/Controller/OCSAuthAPIController.php#L143) to later execute `GetSharedSecret`.
4. When B's cron next runs, it executes [`GetSharedSecret`](https://github.com/nextcloud/server/blob/daf3b29572921562abcb700052c1de

def preprocess_handler(inference_record, logger):

This panic (`zrl_destroy` VERIFY in `dnode_buf_evict_async` on 0.8.4) has no reproducer, the dnode and zrlock code has changed a lot since then, and as noted in the thread a fresh report on a current version is needed to make progress. comments.body:
It looks like the postgres container does not have the permissions to modify [the danbooru-data volume](https://github.com/danbooru/danbooru/blob/master/docker-compose.yaml#L93).  
Just throwing random guesses here, but how are you launching docker? Is the user you're launching docker-compose with in the docker group? If not, is your docker installation configured to be rootless (https://docs.docker.com/engine/security/rootless/)? Have you tried deleting and recreating that volume (if this is your first time running, if you have an existing installation don't do that or it'll nuke the data)?
My user is already in the `docker` group, but nothing worked. I also tried appending `user: root` into the postgres service and force-recreated the whole thing, but to no avail.

user: root in my experience is a bad idea because it modifies the permission of whatever it's touching in the actual filesystem.

If you do `ls -ltrah /var/lib/docker/volumes/danbooru-data` what do you see? There should be a folder in there assigned to the docker group. Try manually removing that physical volume and see if that fixes it.

If that doesn't work either, try setting the mount for postgres to an actual folder. Something like 

```
    volumes:
      - "/path/to/a/folder/you/own:/var/lib/postgresql/data"
```

> If that doesn't work either, try setting the mount for postgres to an actual folder.

I tried this method, and now it's working properly. Thank you very much!

I ran into this trivial problem early on though:

```shell
danbooru_docker-danbooru-1  | rails aborted!
danbooru_docker-danbooru-1  | ActiveRecord::ConnectionNotEstablished: connection to server at "postgres" (172.18.0.4), port 5432 failed: Connection refused
danbooru_docker-danbooru-1  | 	Is the server running on that host and accepting TCP/IP connections?
```

But all I had to do was run `docker-compose up` one more time, and now it's working just fine.

---

Before I close this issue though, I have one more question. I actually placed my docker images on a custom location instead of `/var/lib/docker`. They are in a Windows partition, and GNOME, when mounting it, gives them the following user/group:

```shell
$ ls -ltrah /path/to/windows/docker/volumes/danbooru-data/
total 4.0K
drwxrwxrwx 1 myusername myusername    0 Jun  9  2020 _data
drwxrwxrwx 1 myusername myusername    0 Jan 21 11:58 .
drwxrwxrwx 1 myusername myusername 4.0K Jan 22 03:05 ..
```

Do you reckon this is why the `chmod` earlier was failing? Why does it only affect the postgres service?

If it's a windows partition does that mean it's NTFS? Maybe postgres is doing something that doesn't interact well with that. I wouldn't be able to tell you the reason but I can think of many things that could wrong, like case insensitiveness, symlinks or other issues with permissions.

Another thing that comes to mind, and it's an issue I've found before, is that maybe the user inside the other docker images is using the same uid as your host user (for example the danbooru docker [creates a single user, "danbooru"](https://github.com/danbooru/danbooru/blob/master/config/docker/Dockerfile.danbooru#L73), which would get the default user ID 1000, and so be[ considered the "same user" as your host user](https://medium.com/@mccode/understanding-how-uid-and-gid-work-in-docker-containers-c37a01d01cf), if it was the first user you created), but postgres is using a different one, so it can't write to those files. This is all just speculation though.

Anyway, glad you figured it out.

title: Avoid requesting new certs inside letsencrypt:enable if valid certs exist
body:
## Description of problem

The `dokku letsencrypt:enable` command seems to request new certificates from the server each time it is executed, regardless of whether or not valid certs already exist for that app. I am not sure if this is the desired behavior or if it makes sense to check whether a valid certificate already exists and not to request a new one if the existing one is fine?

We use `letsencrypt:enable` in our CI scripts during automatic deployment of review branches (which are being updated several times a day). It works fine for the first 5 commits, but then we run into rate limits (see results below). I am aware that we could extend our scripts to somehow check whether the branch was already deployed in the past and use letsencrypt:auto-renew instead, but it sounds way more complicated than implementing one additional check inside `letsencrypt:enable`.

### How reproducible

1. Create a new app or clone an existing app
2. Run `letsencrypt:enable` for that app 1st time (succeeds)
3. Run `letsencrypt:enable` for that app 2nd time (succeeds)
4. Run `letsencrypt:enable` for that app 3rd time (succeeds)
5. Run `letsencrypt:enable` for that app 4th time (succeeds)
6. Run `letsencrypt:enable` for that app 5th time (succeeds)
7. Run `letsencrypt:enable` for that app 6th time (fails):

I would definitely take an MR. Some notes:

- It should take into account the new functionality in `post-domains-update`. That should probably _always_ request a new cert, or at least check if all domains are covered.
- There should be a way to force-refresh the certificates (either via a flag or a new command).

> There should be a way to force-refresh the certificates (either via a flag or a new command).

title: Backend looses its workers and stops running jobs after a while
body:
## Expected Behavior

We expect jobs like "discoverall", "macwalk" and "arpwalk" to be run according to the configured schedules.

## Current Behavior

After starting the backend, jobs are being run fine for quite a while (at least several days). After some unknown time, jobs are not being run any more - we can see that the timestamps for last_discover, last_macsuck and last_arpnip are not updated for any device any more.

## Possible Solution

Not sure. We have been running for a long time (months? years?) with a cron job that just restarts the netdisco-backend every night, but that's not a real solution.

## Steps to Reproduce (for bugs)

We have not been able to actively reproduce. If we don't restart the backend on a daily basis, it will take somewhere between a couple of days to a month at maximum before the backend fails to run jobs.

When jobs aren't run any more, we don't see anything in the logs/backend.log pointing to something that went wrong.

It appears that the "nd2 master" process is dead and no worker processes are active any more, when the issues starts; a `ps -ef | grep netdisco` output looks like this:

```
netdisco@linux786:~/logs$ ps -ef | grep netdisco
netdisco 2362887       1  0 Jul04 ?        00:19:30 netdisco-backend
netdisco 2362888 2362887  0 Jul04 ?        00:23:14 [nd2: master] <defunct>

```
For comparison, the same output on our test server with nightly restarts of the backend looks like this:
```

netdisco 1277288 1152782  0 10:51 ?        00:00:00 nd2: #7 poll: idle
netdisco 1277296 1152782  1 10:51 ?        00:00:00 nd2: #8 poll: idle
```


## Context
<!--- How has this issue affected you? What are you trying to accomplish? -->
<!--- Providing context helps us come up with a solution that is most useful in the real world -->
We're using Netdisco to keep an accurate inventory. Lots of scripts in our network depend on Netdisco for an up-to-date inventory, eg for which devices to pull stats, backup configs, check and modify port settings, etc. Having stale data in Netdisco makes all the other scripts less reliable.


## Your Environment
<!--- Include as many relevant details about the environment you experienced the bug in -->
* Netdisco version used: 2.070001
* SNMP::Info version used: 3.95

## Config info (deployment.yml)
<!--- if possible include all options you added to your deployment.yml file, since -->
<!--- some options can change the behaviour in drastic ways -->
Most relevant parts:
```
# daemon will keep netdisco up to date on this schedule

  discoverall:
    when: '5 * * * *'

    when:
      min: 20

    when: '0 8,13,21 * * *'

    when: '20 23 * * *'

# number of SNMP pollers to run in parallel (in netdisco-daemon)

  pollers: 20

# amount parallel DNS resolution for node names
# `````````````````````````````````````````````
dns:
  max_outstanding: 50
```

Not related to any s

What's interesting to me, is that this is the nd2-master process, which is `netdisco-backend-fg` where the actual job queue lives (and not the other child processes which put and pick jobs on/off the queue, or workers doing jobs). So I wonder if it's a bug in the queueing library or the way we're using it. Being `<defunct>` would indicate it crashed.

Would it be at all possible to run `netdisco-backend-fg` instead of `netdisco-backend` for a few days, and watch it crash? So using something like screen/tmux and tee to grab any dying gasp output. I appreciate this might be difficult as you use it operationally.

I will also have a look to see if we can get `netdisco-backend` to restart `netdisco-backend-fg` either periodically (yuck) or by detecting the failure itself (slightly less but still yuck).

On both my servers, the crash hasn't happened yet. We're monitoring them closely, for active process counts as well as median age for the last_{discover,macsuck,arpnip} age - so I expect that we'll notice quickly when one of them dies again.

As reported I **think** this is a manifestation of a bug in the (latest, as of 2024-10-28) Ingres Adapter (which supports SQLAlchemy 2.x and most of 1.x)  - see https://github.com/ActianCorp/sqlalchemy-ingres/issues/68 this is NOT a problem with older versions of the Ingres Adapter which have full SQLAlchemy version 1.x support. Either use an older version of the Ingres SQLAlchemy Adapter that fully supports SQA version 1.0 .. or SuperSet needs to be updated to use SQLAlchemy version 2.

The trigger for this is the use of SQLAlchemy version 1.x, rather than the 2.x series. I'm note clear how much work it would take to update SuperSet (but I do not think just bumping the version dependency is enough).
This has been silent for quite a while. Is anyone here still facing this, particularly in 4.1.2 or 5.0.0rc2?

@priyank-stack are you able retest with latest?
CC @hab6
We haven't heard back in quite some time, so I'll assume all is well and close this out. Holler if it needs revisiting/reopening on 5.0/`master`

$ python -m nuitka --version

```
Nuitka was installed via pip inside a Poetry-managed virtual environment. Python was installed using pyenv.

### Problem Description

I am encountering a runtime error when running a standalone Nuitka-built executable that includes apscheduler. The script works as expected when run directly using Python.

### Error message:
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/tmp/onefile_1183401_1735607435_403686/testbuild.py", line 2, in <module>
    from apscheduler.schedulers.asyncio import AsyncIOScheduler

  File "<frozen importlib._bootstrap>", line 680, in _load_unlocked

  File "/tmp/onefile_1183401_1735607435_403686/apscheduler/schedulers/base.py", line 87, in BaseScheduler
KeyError: 'apscheduler.triggers'
```

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Install apscheduler via poetry:
```
poetry add apscheduler
poetry install
poetry shell
```
2. Example script (testbuild.py):
```python
import asyncio
from apscheduler.schedulers.asyncio import AsyncIOScheduler
from apscheduler.jobstores.memory import MemoryJobStore
from apscheduler.executors.asyncio import AsyncIOExecutor


async def test_func():
    print("Test function is running!")
    return True

def run_scheduler():
    jobstores = {
        'test_store': MemoryJobStore(),
    }
    executors = {'default': AsyncIOExecutor()}
    scheduler = AsyncIOScheduler(
        jobstores=jobstores,
        executors=executors,
    )

    scheduler.add_job(
        id='test_func',
        func=test_func,
        trigger="cron",
        jobstore='test_store',
        second='*',
    )

    scheduler.start()

async def main():
    print("Scheduler is running...")
    try:
        run_scheduler()
        while True:
            await asyncio.sleep(1)
    except (KeyboardInterrupt, SystemExit):
        print("Shutting down scheduler...")
        scheduler.shutdown()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        asyncio.run(main())
    except RuntimeError as e:
        print(f"RuntimeError: {e}")
        loop = asyncio.new_event_loop()
        asyncio.set_event_loop(loop)
        loop.run_until_complete(main())
```
### Nuitka build command:
```shell
nuitka \
  --standalone \
  testbuild.py
```
### Run the resulting binary:
./testbuild.dist/testbuild.bin

### Expected Behavior

The program should execute as it does when run directly with Python, printing Job executed! per seconds.

### Observed Behavior

The standalone executable crashes with the error:

ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'apscheduler.triggers'

### Additional Information

1. Running with --onefile produces the same error.
2. Including   --include-package=apscheduler.triggers did not resolve the issue.
3. APScheduler version: 3.10.4

comments.body: @korpa I think you're missing the `--from` flag, otherwise, Pop will want to open a tui to get that info

I think, this is not necessary as I'm using SMTP for sending and have set following env variables:

```
POP_SMTP_HOST
POP_SMTP_PORT
POP_SMTP_USERNAME
POP_SMTP_PASSWORD
```
In this case POP uses `POP_SMTP_USERNAME` as `From:` address.

If I run the same script manually from bash, it works.
I just added the `--from` flag to double check if it really is the issue. Sadly nothing changes. I still get the "TTY error".

I found a workaround for this. For some reason, when without TTY (i.e. cron, pipeline, etc.) `pop` somehow ignores `--body` flag.

This worked for me in a pipeline:
```
echo "message body" | pop ....
```
I believe this little PR should fix the problem: https://github.com/charmbracelet/pop/pull/124

Maybe?

Dokku on docker mounts the /var/lib/dokku directory in /mnt/dokku inside the container.

From [the docs](https://dokku.com/docs/getting-started/install/docker/), the startup command is:
```
docker container run \
  --env DOKKU_HOSTNAME=dokku.me \
  --env DOKKU_HOST_ROOT=/var/lib/dokku/home/dokku \
  --env DOKKU_LIB_HOST_ROOT=/var/lib/dokku/var/lib/dokku \
  --name dokku \
  --publish 3022:22 \
  --publish 8080:80 \
  --publish 8443:443 \
  --volume /var/lib/dokku:/mnt/dokku \
  --volume /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \
  dokku/dokku:0.30.10
```

After a short look, the problem was introduced in this PR:

https://github.com/dokku/dokku-postgres/pull/260

The error is here:
https://github.com/dokku/dokku-postgres/pull/260/files#diff-edc2d49bc616ba015b53812dab17c94cbb85dd694d9f08b82e5cd8ec8467c378R5

the cd command fails silently because there's no `set -e`, and the key is created in the current directory.

The cd fails because `postgres_service_dir` is set to `/var/lib/dokku/var/lib/dokku/services/[name_of_db]`, that doesn't exist.

... but, why is the folder `/var/lib/dokku/var/lib/dokku` in the first place? Is this a bug?


PR upcoming if I figure this out.

TL;DR if you need this to work, just use an older version of the plugin (i.e. 1.33.1)
The first service host Roy should probably be service root.

The problem is solved with the command:
`dokku ps:scale %my_app_name% web=0 worker=1`

but I think that this is a bug, because the web section was not indicated in the Procfile

I _think_ this is a bug but I feel like I've looked at this exact issue several times over the years. I should have time later this week to go over git history/docs to figure out what the correct workflow is.

Okay I see what happened. We've always required a `web` process to start, but I think in the past before #4508, we may have skipped processes that do not exist.

In any case, we won't automatically scale up anything other than web:

> For initial app deploys, Dokku will default to starting a single `web` process for each app. This process may be defined within the `Procfile` or as the `CMD` (for Dockerfile or Docker image deploys). Scaling of the `web` process - and all other processes - may be managed via `ps:scale` or the `formations` key in the `app.json` file either before or after the initial deploy.

So in all cases, you'd still need to at least scale your worker up.

---

That said, we should probably _not_ scale up `web` if it doesn't exist in the `Procfile`. The tricky thing is that Dockerfile-based deploys sometimes don't have a `Procfile` and instead specify the command via a CMD (or custom entrypoint). Also, sometimes the process is injected from the buildpack for CNB/Herokuish apps. This makes it tricky to always skip the `web` process.

Let me think on how we should do this.
Closing as there is a pull request open. If tests pass, it'll go into the next minor.
